pr_body:
### Description

close https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/18129

NOTE: I started trying to bundle the chokidar types instead of inlining it, but it didn't work out as easily because chokidar's types includes a lot of internal stuff, which causes bundling issues, type compat issues, and large bundle size. At the end it's better to keep inlining it.

Due to explorations above, I've tweaked our code to work a little differently which I'll make comments below explaining

---

It also looks like we can remove the anymatch types that was used by chokidar before. I'm thinking perhaps that can be a follow-up.
pr_comments:
Of course it has to be windows 🥲 I did get that error locally while developing, but the added `await page.goto(viteTestUrl)` fixed it for me. Not sure why not for windows.

EDIT: Looks like it's not necessarily windows now.

I'm able to reproduce locally sometimes by updating the `vitest.config.e2e.ts` with:
1. `procese.env.CI = true`
2. `test.minWorkers: 1` and `test.maxWorkers: 1`

And after adding some loggings, here's what I got:
```bash
stdout | playground/hmr/__tests__/hmr.spec.ts > should hmr when file is deleted and restored
edit child

watch change /Users/bjorn/Work/oss/vite/playground-temp/hmr/file-delete-restore/child.js

edit parent
delete child

watch change /Users/bjorn/Work/oss/vite/playground-temp/hmr/file-delete-restore/parent.js

add child
edit parent

watch change /Users/bjorn/Work/oss/vite/playground-temp/hmr/file-delete-restore/parent.js
watch change /Users/bjorn/Work/oss/vite/playground-temp/hmr/file-delete-restore/child.js
```

> `add child/parent` and `edit child/parent` are logged from the test. `watch change/add/delete` are logged from the fs watcher hooks.

From what I can tell, chokidar (or node fs) is collapsing the `delete child` and `add child` into a single file `change` event rather than 2 `delete` and `add` event. Perhaps it's related to https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1361

Adding a timeout seems to make it more stable, though a bit unfortunate to have it. What's described in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18453#issuecomment-2437063937 was causing the issue, and a timeout after the initial delete needs to be long enough for the fs to detect a deletion.

issue_context.title: Upgrade to chokidar v4
issue_context.body:
### Description

Chokidar v4 is out now so can upgrade to it

### Suggested solution

Should be done as part of a major since it's a bit breaking. Vite isn't using globs which were removed and disables them with disableGlobbing, but plugins can unfortunately hack around it [like this](https://github.com/antfu/vite-plugin-restart/blob/43461b5f362e31944502cefdc45ef9c1f3ebf9eb/src/index.ts#L67)

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

Rollup will upgrade in 5.0: https://github.com/rollup/rollup/issues/5656#issuecomment-2357504813

### Validations

- [X] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [X] Read the [docs](https://vitejs.dev/guide).
- [X] Check that there isn't already an issue that request the same feature to avoid creating a duplicate.
comments:
> Vite isn't using globs which were removed

Vite supports glob in `ignored` option.
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c1ed8a595a02ec7f8f5a8d23f97b2f21d3834ab1/packages/vite/src/node/watch.ts#L58-L64

just a side note, glob is not directly supported by chokidar but they do mention that it's supported in other ways by reading glob from `node:fs` or `node-glob` see the Chokidar upgrading section for that

https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar?tab=readme-ov-file#upgrading

review_comments: 📝 Note to reviewers: chokidar no longer uses `fsevents` (uses `fs.watch` for macos as well)

This will break these: https://github.com/ElMassimo/vite-plugin-full-reload/blob/00045424209f8f9bef260047da1e9a73afd78f43/src/index.ts#L48, https://github.com/search?q=watch.disableGlobbing+NOT+is%3Afork&type=code
Probably fine but just to point it out.

I removed `NoopWatcher` in favor of patching the chokidar watcher with `watcher.add = function () {  return this }` as `FSWatcher.options` now return a resolved option (non-nullable) which we'd have to copy over from chokidar if we retain `NoopWatcher`.

It was also initially hard to make types happy because `chokidar` export types for `FSWatcher` contained a bunch of internal properties making `implements` unhappy. 

This trick could be easier to maintain in the long run instead.
but doesn't it start watching when you call `watch`? 🤔
In resolveWatchOptions I added a config to ignore every path if this is null, so no fs.watch will happen but there will be a chokidar fs watcher instance that does nothing.

It was also possible to do with the previous watcher, but I went with a noop watcher specifically to avoid having a running process. Even if every path is ignored, it will still try to check them and have an expensive watcher do nothing.
I don't know if it's exactly expensive. The alternative like before is harder to implement if we want to stick with it.

> The alternative like before is harder to implement if we want to stick with it.

How hard can it be to implement a noop? 

> I don't know if it's exactly expensive

Would you call `fs.watch` in your every project just for lols? Why start a watcher to ignore it?
As I mentioned before, the ignore will already block any fs.watch from happening in the first place. Happy to be proven wrong here.

> How hard can it be to implement a noop?

Ok, I checked - and the only thing that changed is the options - Is it really worth it to start a new watcher every time `createServer` is called just to avoid adding mocked options?

> As I mentioned before, the ignore will already block any fs.watch from happening in the first place. Happy to be proven wrong here.

I don't see any filtering happening to files passed down to `add` which is called when `chockidr.watch(paths)` is called (these paths are even removed from ignored 🤔 ): 

https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/blob/97894d36657c8e4571bd1a07fb6e2a3f50f7019d/src/index.ts#L442

Seems like ignoring happens when it's already watching. But maybe using `.watch([])` will work already.
We can also close it immediately maybe. This will always ignore anything
I've added more guards here: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18521

I did some manual testing and can confirm that `fs.watch`isn't being called with this implementation. It's being blocked here: https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/blob/97894d36657c8e4571bd1a07fb6e2a3f50f7019d/src/handler.ts#L682-L685

But I don't mind that PR adding some more guards to skip things.

I removed this export because initially it wasn't exported by `chokidar`. It feels kinda rare to use this and I don't see it [publicly used anywhere](https://github.com/search?q=import+AwaitWriteFinishOptions+vite+NOT+is%3Afork&type=code) on github. So I figured to remove this.
